more.def: A machine that blows out a strong stream of air.
examples: Dad used a leaf blower to clear the yard.
The snow blower cleared the driveway.
The blower hummed all morning.

easy.def: A fish that puffs up like a ball.
examples: The blowfish puffs.
A blowfish is round.
The blowfish got big.

more.def: A fish that can puff up its body like a ball when it is frightened.
examples: The blowfish puffed up when the diver came near.
A blowfish swallows water to look big.
Blowfish live in warm seas.

easy.def: The hole on a whale's head that it breathes through.
examples: The whale has a blowhole.
Water sprayed from the blowhole.
A blowhole is on top.

more.def: The hole on top of a whale's or dolphin's head that it uses to breathe.
examples: The whale sprayed water out of its blowhole.
A dolphin breathes through its blowhole.
The blowhole opened as the whale surfaced.

easy.def: A tool that makes a very hot flame.
examples: The worker used a blowtorch.
A blowtorch is hot.
The blowtorch melted metal.

more.def: A tool that shoots out a very hot flame, used for melting or cutting metal.
examples: The welder used a blowtorch to join the metal.
The chef used a small blowtorch to brown the top of the dessert.
Only adults should use a blowtorch.

easy.def: The thick layer of fat under the skin of a whale or seal.
examples: A whale has blubber.
Blubber keeps seals warm.
The blubber is thick.

more.def: The thick layer of fat under the skin of whales and seals that keeps them warm in cold water.
examples: The whale's thick blubber keeps it warm in the icy sea.
Seals have a layer of blubber under their skin.
Blubber was once used to make oil for lamps.

easy.def: Having the color of the sky.
examples: The sky is blue.
She has blue eyes.
My coat is blue.

more.def: Having the color of a clear sky or the sea.
examples: He painted the walls bright blue.
She wore a blue dress to the party.
The blue water sparkled in the sun.

easy.def: The color of the sky.
examples: Blue is my favorite color.
The sea is a deep blue.
Mix blue and yellow to make green.

more.def: The color of a clear sky or the deep sea.
examples: The artist mixed blue and white for the sky.
The sea was a deep blue.
Blue looks nice with yellow.

easy.def: A small flower shaped like a bell, usually blue.
examples: A bluebell grew in the woods.
The bluebell is blue.
We picked a bluebell.

more.def: A wild plant with small blue flowers shaped like bells.
examples: A carpet of bluebells covered the forest floor in spring.
The bluebell nodded in the soft breeze.
We found a patch of bluebells near the stream.

easy.def: A small, round, blue fruit.
examples: I ate a blueberry.
The blueberry is sweet.
Blueberries are in the muffin.

more.def: A small, round, sweet berry that is dark blue and grows on bushes.
examples: I ate a blueberry muffin for breakfast.
We picked blueberries from the bush behind the barn.
Blueberries are full of vitamins and taste good in pancakes.

easy.def: A small bird with blue feathers.
examples: A bluebird sat on the fence.
The bluebird sang.
I saw a bluebird.

more.def: A small songbird that has bright blue feathers on its back.
examples: A bluebird built a nest in the old fence post.
The bluebird's bright blue back flashed in the sun.
Bluebirds eat insects and berries.

easy.def: A kind of country music played on banjos and fiddles.
examples: We like bluegrass.
The bluegrass band played.
Bluegrass is fast.

more.def: A style of American folk music played on banjos, fiddles and guitars.
examples: The bluegrass band played fast banjo songs.
We danced to bluegrass music at the fair.
Bluegrass started in the mountains of the South.

easy.def: A plan that shows how to build something.
examples: The builder looked at the blueprint.
The blueprint shows the rooms.
We drew a blueprint.

more.def: A detailed plan or drawing that shows how something will be built.
examples: The builder studied the blueprint for the new house.
The blueprint shows where each room and window will go.
We drew a blueprint of our clubhouse before we started building.

easy.def: A feeling of being sad.
examples: I have the blues.
The rain gave her the blues.
He had the Monday blues.

more.def: A feeling of sadness.
examples: The rainy day gave me the blues.
She had the blues when her friend moved.
A funny movie chased the blues away.

easy.def: A slow, sad kind of music.
examples: I like the blues.
He plays the blues.
The band played the blues.

more.def: A style of slow music that began in the United States and has a sad sound.
examples: He plays the blues on his guitar.
The band played the blues all night.
I like to listen to the blues on Sundays.

easy.def: A high hill with a straight side.
examples: We stood on the bluff.
The bluff overlooked the sea.
The bluff is tall.

more.def: A high, steep cliff or hillside, often by the sea or a river.
examples: We stood on the bluff and watched the waves.
A tall bluff rose above the river.
The house sits on a bluff above the sea.

easy.def: To pretend so that others believe you.
examples: He bluffed in the game.
She tried to bluff her way through.
I bluffed that I knew.

more.def: To trick people by pretending to be stronger or to know more than you do.
examples: She bluffed during the card game.
He tried to bluff his way out of trouble.
I bluffed when I did not know the answer.

easy.def: A big, silly mistake.
examples: That was a blunder.
I made a blunder.
A big blunder.

more.def: A careless or foolish mistake.
examples: Forgetting my lunch was a blunder.
The player made a blunder and dropped the ball.
The teacher laughed at his blunder, and so did he.

easy.def: To make a big, silly mistake.
examples: I blundered.
He blundered in the test.
She blundered into the wall.

more.def: To make a careless mistake, or to move clumsily.
examples: I blundered when I added the numbers the wrong way.
He blundered through the dark room and bumped the chair.
The team blundered and lost the lead.

easy.def: Not sharp.
examples: The knife is blunt.
The pencil is blunt.
I need a blunt pair of scissors.

more.def: Not sharp or pointed at the end.
examples: The scissors were blunt and could not cut the paper well.
A blunt pencil makes a thick line.
Children's safety scissors have blunt tips.

easy.def: Saying exactly what you think, without being gentle.
examples: He was blunt about the test.
Her answer was blunt.
The coach was blunt.

more.def: Speaking in a plain, direct way that may seem rude.
examples: He gave a blunt answer and told us the truth.
The coach was blunt and said we needed more practice.
She is blunt, so you always know what she is thinking.

easy.def: Something you cannot see clearly.
examples: The photo was a blur.
The bike was a blur.
Everything was a blur.

more.def: Something that looks fuzzy and unclear because it is moving fast or you cannot focus on it.
examples: The race car was just a blur as it sped past.
Without my glasses, the writing on the board is a blur.
The days at camp passed in a happy blur.

easy.def: To make something hard to see clearly.
examples: Tears blurred my eyes.
Rain blurred the window.
Steam blurs my glasses.

more.def: To make something look fuzzy or unclear, or to become hard to see clearly.
examples: Steam from the soup blurred my glasses.
The rain blurred the lights of the cars outside.
Fast moving legs blurred the picture of the runner.

easy.def: Not clear to see.
examples: The photo is blurry.
My eyes feel blurry.
It was blurry in the fog.

more.def: Not clear or sharp to look at, so the edges are hard to see.
examples: The photo was blurry because the camera shook.
The mountains looked blurry in the fog.
Without her glasses, the words on the page were blurry.

easy.def: To say something quickly without thinking.
examples: I blurt out an answer.
He blurted a word.
She blurted the secret.

more.def: To say something suddenly without thinking first.
examples: I blurted out the answer before she finished.
He blurted the secret by mistake.
Do not blurt out answers in class.

easy.def: To turn red in the face.
examples: I blush when I am shy.
She blushed.
He blushed with shame.

more.def: To get red cheeks because you feel shy or embarrassed.
examples: I blushed when everyone sang to me.
She blushed at the compliment.
He blushed when he forgot her name.

easy.def: To talk in a loud way to show off.
examples: He blustered and boasted.
The wind blustered.
She blustered about.

more.def: To speak in a loud, angry or boastful way that does not mean much, or to blow in rough gusts.
examples: He blustered about how he would win.
The wind blustered around the old house.
The man blustered angrily but no one was scared.

easy.def: Windy and rough.
examples: It was a blustery day.
A blustery wind.
The blustery weather.

more.def: Windy and rough, with strong gusts.
examples: It was a blustery day, so we flew kites.
A blustery wind blew our hats away.
The blustery weather rattled the windows.
